q: Your organization wants to enforce naming conventions for Microsoft Entra groups to ensure consistency. For example, all group names should start with the department name (e.g., 'HR-'). How can you achieve this?
options: Use Azure Policies to define naming rules for groups.
Implement a PowerShell script that runs daily to enforce the naming convention.
Use Group Naming Policy in Microsoft Entra ID and configure prefix/suffix rules.
Manually rename each group as they are created.
exp: Use Group Naming Policy in Microsoft Entra ID and configure prefix/suffix rules.

q: You have an Azure subscription that contains a virtual network named VNet1. You plan to deploy a virtual machine named VM1 to be used as a network inspection appliance. You need to ensure that all network traffic passes through VM1. What should you do?
A user reports they cannot access certain Microsoft 365 services despite having an assigned license. You find the user's license is disabled. What is the most likely cause?
options: The user's account has been disabled in Microsoft Entra ID.
The license was assigned through a group, but the service plan for that license is disabled.
The user's role does not permit them to use the licensed services.
The license has not yet been synchronized with the Microsoft 365 portal.
exp: The license was assigned through a group, but the service plan for that license is disabled.

q: You need to ensure that all storage accounts across multiple subscriptions under a single management group have secure transfer enabled. What is the most efficient way to achieve this?
options: Assign the policy to each resource group individually.
Assign the policy at the management group level.
Assign the policy to a single subscription and replicate the setup.
Use Azure Monitor to track non-compliant storage accounts.
exp: Assign the policy at the management group level.

q: A developer tries to delete a container within a storage account that has a 'Delete' lock applied but encounters an error. What is the reason?
options: The Delete lock applies to all sub-resources of the storage account, including containers.
The developer lacks Azure RBAC permissions to delete the container.
Containers are not affected by resource locks unless applied directly.
The lock is incorrectly configured and should only apply to the storage account itself.
exp: The Delete lock applies to all sub-resources of the storage account, including containers.

q: You want to make a new user created in your on-premises Active Directory available in Azure AD immediately. Which PowerShell command should you run?
Which Azure AD role enables a user to manage all groups in your Teams tenants, and also assign other admin roles?
Your company financial controller wants to identify which billing department each Azure resource belongs to. Which approach enables this requirement?
options: Track resource usage in a spreadsheet
Place the resources in different regions.
Apply a tag to each resource that includes the associated billing department.
Place the resources in different subscriptions.
exp: Apply a tag to each resource that includes the associated billing department.

q: Your company has several departments, each with its own virtual machines (VMs) in a single resource group named RG1. You need to associate each VM with its department for cost allocation without restructuring RG1. What should you do?
options: Create Azure Management Groups for each department.
Create separate resource groups for each department.
Modify the configuration settings of each virtual machine.
Assign tags to each virtual machine.
exp: Assign tags to each virtual machine.

q: You need to ensure that User1 can assign the Reader role for VNET1 to other users. User1 currently has the Reader and Security Admin roles. What should you do?
options: Assign User1 the Network Contributor role for VNET1.
Assign User1 the Owner role for VNET1.
Assign User1 the Contributor role for RG1.
Add User1 to the User Access Administrator role at the subscription level.
exp: Assign User1 the Owner role for VNET1.

q: A company needs to create a storage account that supports file shares across several VMs, allows archiving, and remains available even if one region goes down. The solution must be cost-effective. Which redundancy type should you choose?
You have an Azure virtual machine named Server1 that runs Windows Server. You need to configure Azure Backup to back up files and folders. What should you install on Server1?
options: The Microsoft Azure Recovery Services (MARS) agent
exp: The Microsoft Azure Recovery Services (MARS) agent

q: You need to transfer 5TB of data to an Azure subscription using an Azure Import/Export job. What can you use as the destination?
You are using AzCopy to copy data to Azure Files. Which authentication method is supported for this operation?
options: Both Microsoft Entra ID and SAS tokens

q: Which storage accounts support moving data to the Archive access tier?
options: Storage accounts configured as LRS, GRS, and RA-GRS.
All storage accounts regardless of redundancy.
exp: Storage accounts configured as LRS, GRS, and RA-GRS.

q: What statement best describes Azure Blob Storage access tiers?
options: The cool access tier is for frequent access of objects in the storage account.
The hot access tier is for storing large amounts of data that's infrequently accessed.
The administrator can switch between hot and cool performance tiers at any time.
The archive tier is for short time of storage.
exp: The administrator can switch between hot and cool performance tiers at any time.

q: What is the maximum number of 'stored access policies' you can create for a single blob container?
You are modifying an ARM template. Which action ensures that a storage account is created before a virtual machine that depends on it?
options: Reorder the resources in the template so the storage account is defined first.
Use a condition to deploy the storage account only if the VM exists.
Add the dependsOn property to the virtual machine resource and reference the storage account.
Place the storage account in a nested template.
exp: Add the dependsOn property to the virtual machine resource and reference the storage account.

q: The admin team needs to know the requirements for storage account names. To what extent does a storage account name need to be unique?
options: The name must be unique within the containing resource group.
The name must be unique within the organization's subscription.
The name must be globally unique.
The name must be unique within the hole tenant.
exp: The name must be globally unique.

options: Move the virtual machine to another Azure subscription

options: Scale up the App Service plan to the Standard (S1) tier or higher.
Scale out the App Service plan to 5 instances.
Modify the application settings of the Web App.
Add a custom domain to the Web App.

q: Your company wants to automate post-deployment configuration tasks (like installing antivirus) on a VM. Which feature should you recommend?
You have an Azure subscription that contains network security groups (NSGs). Which two resources can be associated with an NSG?
Which VM size is most cost-effective for batch processing workloads that run for only 2 hours daily and can be interrupted?
You have three virtual networks: VNET1 (196.162.0.0/24), VNET2 (10.10.0.0/24), and VNET3 (196.162.0.0/16). Which networks can be peered?
options: VNET1 and VNET2, and VNET2 and VNET3.
All three networks can be peered together.
No peering is possible due to address overlapping.

You have a public load balancer balancing ports 80 and 443. You need to ensure a user is consistently routed to the same web server every time they access it. What should you configure?
options: Session persistence to Client IP (or Client IP and Protocol).
exp: Session persistence to Client IP (or Client IP and Protocol).

You have four Azure virtual machines that have the following configurations: VM1: Subnet: Subnet1 Network card: NIC1 NIC1 is assigned to NSG2. VM2: Subnet: Subnet1 Network card: NIC2 NIC2 is assigned to NSG3. VM3: Subnet: Subnet3 Network card: NIC3 NIC3 is assigned to NSG3. You need to connect an on-premises network to Azure using a Site-to-Site VPN. What is the correct sequence of actions?
options: Deploy VPN Gateway -> Create Local Network Gateway -> Create VPN Connection.
Deploy Gateway Subnet -> Deploy VPN Gateway -> Create Local Network Gateway -> Create VPN Connection.
Create VPN Connection -> Deploy VPN Gateway -> Create Local Network Gateway.
Deploy Gateway Subnet -> Create Local Network Gateway -> Deploy VPN Gateway.
exp: Deploy Gateway Subnet -> Deploy VPN Gateway -> Create Local Network Gateway -> Create VPN Connection.

q: You have three virtual machines (VM1, VM2, VM3) in a resource group. A new admin is hired, and they need to be able to modify settings on VM3. They shouldn't be able to make changes to VM1 or VM2. How can you implement RBAC to minimize administrative overhead?
options: Assign the admin to the Contributor role on the resource group.
Assign the admin to the Contributor role on VM3.
Move VM3 to a new resource group, and then assign the admin to the Owner role on VM3.
Move VM3 to a new subscription, and then assign the Owner role.
exp: Assign the admin to the Contributor role on VM3.

q: How is Azure Virtual Network peering best described?
options: Traffic between virtual networks is kept on the Microsoft backbone network.
Virtual network peering disrupts other resources.
Peered virtual networks must be in the same region.
Peering is like DNS server at each subscription.
exp: Traffic between virtual networks is kept on the Microsoft backbone network.

q: You need to deploy Azure Firewall to VNET1. Subnet1 has 15 VMs, and Subnet2 has no VMs. What must you do first?
options: Add a new subnet named AzureFirewallSubnet to VNET1.
Modify the subnet mask of Subnet2.
Add a service endpoint to Subnet2.
exp: Add a new subnet named AzureFirewallSubnet to VNET1.

You need to create an alert when more than two error events are logged to the system event log on VM1 within an hour. What is required?
options: Install the Microsoft Monitoring Agent (or Azure Monitor Agent) on VM1 and use a Log Analytics workspace.
Create an Azure Storage account and configure SAS tokens.

q: A VM is infected with ransomware. You need to restore it to a clean state. What is the safest recommended action?
options: Restore the VM after deleting the infected VM.
Restore the VM to a new Azure virtual machine.
Restore the VM to any VM within the same subscription.
Restore the VM to an on-premises device.
exp: Restore the VM to a new Azure virtual machine.
